summary.name: Haiku macro/sector rotation
summary.strategy: Position for the 2026 macro backdrop centered on the AI and semiconductor super-cycle. Overweight semiconductor infrastructure (NVDA, TSM, AMD, ASML) at the core of AI capex, combined with AI-beneficiary mega-cap software and cloud (MSFT, GOOG, AAPL) plus growth (TSLA), with defensive diversification (UNH, COST) for risk management. Equal-weight across 10 positions to capture macro rotation into AI-driven capex cycle.

summary.name: Haiku deep value
summary.strategy: Deep value focus on companies trading well below intrinsic value on P/E, price-to-book, and FCF metrics. Targets operationally sound businesses with strong dividends and cash generation positioned for valuation mean reversion and multiple expansion in H1 2026.

summary.name: Haiku price momentum
summary.strategy: Capture the strongest 12-month price momentum in US equities, concentrating in AI infrastructure, semiconductors, and cloud computing leaders that have driven market outperformance through 2024-2025.

summary.name: Sonnet contrarian turnarounds
summary.strategy: Equal-weight basket of beaten-down names with identifiable 2026 catalysts: management/strategic resets, restructuring, product cycle reboots, or sector mean-reversion after heavy 2024-2025 selloffs.

summary.name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
summary.strategy: Concentrated, equal-weight basket of leading AI infrastructure and platform companies expected to drive and capture the ongoing AI capex/adoption cycle through 1H26: semiconductor/compute leaders, hyperscaler cloud/AI platforms, and enterprise software beneficiaries.

summary.name: Haiku global diversification via US-listed ADRs and ETFs
summary.strategy: Emerging market recovery positioning via Chinese tech leaders (TCEHY, BABA) and emerging markets ETF, combined with semiconductor infrastructure plays (ASML, TSM, ARM) poised to benefit from ongoing AI capex buildout. Complemented by developed-market quality companies (SAP, NVO, NFLX) and international diversification through regional ETFs. The portfolio leverages geographic diversification and sector exposure uncorrelated with S&P 500 concentration.

summary.name: Sonnet dividend growth and income
summary.strategy: Equal-weight basket of high-quality dividend growers and income compounders spanning defensive and cyclical sectors, emphasizing durable cash flows, long dividend growth streaks, and reasonable valuations to outperform the S&P 500 over a 6-month window while providing downside ballast via income and quality.

summary.name: Sonnet deep value
summary.strategy: Deep value equal-weight basket of US large/mid-caps trading at low P/E, low P/B, and high FCF yield, screened from pre-2026-cutoff knowledge across financials, energy, autos, healthcare, and industrials — sectors chronically out of favor but generating strong cash flow. Avoids high-multiple growth/tech to maximize valuation margin of safety versus the cap-weighted S&P 500.

summary.name: Sonnet growth at a reasonable price
summary.strategy: GARP: quality growth companies with durable competitive advantages, trading at reasonable multiples relative to their growth rates (as of Jan 2026 knowledge). Mix of large-cap tech compounders, healthcare/industrial growers, and financials benefiting from secular trends, avoiding the most extreme high-multiple hypergrowth names while still capturing above-market earnings growth.

summary.name: Haiku contrarian turnarounds
summary.strategy: Value recovery in beaten-down mega-caps across AI semiconductors, streaming profitability inflection, fintech repositioning, and automotive electrification. Target operational catalysts and mean-reversion driven by near-term product launches, cost discipline initiatives, and secular growth thesis maturation through H1 2026.

summary.name: Sonnet macro/sector rotation
summary.strategy: Positioning for a 2026 macro backdrop of continued Fed easing, a softer dollar, sticky-but-moderating inflation, and reaccelerating global industrial/capex activity (AI infrastructure buildout, grid/power investment, reshoring). Rotate into rate-sensitive cyclicals (financials, homebuilders/industrials), commodities/gold as a dollar-debasement and geopolitical hedge, international/EM equities benefiting from a weaker USD, and power/infrastructure plays tied to AI-driven electricity demand, while trimming pure mega-cap-tech concentration in favor of broader participation (small/mid caps via financials and industrials).

summary.name: Opus Value

summary.name: Haiku quality compounders
summary.strategy: Concentrated portfolio of highest-quality US businesses with strong competitive moats, high ROIC, and fortress balance sheets. Heavy positioning in AI-driven software and semiconductors, paired with ecosystem platforms and premium financial services. Emphasis on companies that compound earnings at high rates through pricing power and capital efficiency.

summary.name: Haiku dividend growth and income
summary.strategy: Equal-weight portfolio of dividend aristocrats and dividend growth stocks spanning sectors. Emphasizes companies with 25+ year dividend increase streaks, strong free cash flow, and proven ability to grow dividends faster than inflation. Includes pure dividend-growth ETF exposure for systematic diversification.

summary.name: Opus Quality Defensive
summary.strategy: quality / low-volatility defensive

summary.name: Haiku growth at a reasonable price
summary.strategy: Focus on high-quality companies with strong earnings growth and competitive moats, primarily in AI infrastructure, cloud platforms, semiconductors, and enterprise software. Equal-weight portfolio emphasizing companies benefiting from AI adoption, cloud infrastructure spending, and digital transformation over 2026.

summary.name: Haiku small/mid-cap growth
summary.strategy: Growth-oriented portfolio targeting fast-growing cloud, AI, and fintech companies in the small-to-mid-cap range. Focus on businesses benefiting from secular trends: cloud migration, AI/ML adoption, cybersecurity spending, and digital transformation. Equal-weighted allocation emphasizes individual growth potential while maintaining sector diversification.

summary.name: Sonnet global diversification via US-listed ADRs and ETFs
summary.strategy: Equal-weight global diversification basket combining broad international/EM ETFs with high-quality individual ADRs across regions and sectors (Europe luxury/industrials, Asia tech/semis, LatAm financials) to capture non-US growth and reduce US concentration risk while aiming to outperform the S&P 500 over a 6-month window.

summary.name: Sonnet price momentum
summary.strategy: Equal-weight basket of the strongest 12-month price momentum names heading into 2026, concentrated in AI infrastructure, semiconductors, and secular growth leaders that led the market through 2025.

summary.name: Sonnet quality compounders
summary.strategy: Equal-weight basket of high-ROIC, wide-moat compounders with strong balance sheets across tech, healthcare, consumer, and financials, aiming to outperform the S&P 500 over a 6-month horizon (Jan-Jul 2026) through quality resilience and secular growth exposure.

summary.name: Sonnet small/mid-cap growth
summary.strategy: Equal-weight basket of high-growth small/mid-cap companies across software, fintech, biotech, industrials and consumer, selected for durable secular tailwinds (AI adoption, automation, digital payments, healthcare innovation) and reasonable momentum heading into 2026, aiming to outpace the large-cap-dominated S&P 500 over a 6-month horizon.
